title: Written contract, trial period, and student notice
summary: Sign the contract before starting work. Title VII of the law of July 3, 1978 provides for a trial period and specific notice requirements.
body: Articles 123 and 124 require an individual written agreement no later than the start of work, with start and end dates. Article 126 allows a student to leave without notice or compensation if a proper written agreement is missing or if mandatory declaration is not made; certain omissions subject the employer to permanent employment contract rules.

Article 127: the first three working days constitute the trial period, with termination possible without notice or compensation. Successive student contracts for the same position do not allow repetition of the trial period.

Article 130: for an engagement not exceeding one month, notice is three days for the employer and one day for the student; beyond that, seven and three days. It begins the Monday following notification. Article 129: after more than seven days of incapacity, the employer may terminate by providing compensation corresponding to the remaining notice period.

title: Mandatory provisions to include in student contract
summary: The contract must describe the position, remuneration, working time, and practical safety information.
body: Indicate the identity, birth date, and address of the parties, contract dates, location, position, daily and weekly hours, remuneration or its calculation, payment date, joint committee, and any lodging provided. Mention application of the law protecting remuneration as well as the duration and conditions of the trial period.

Add schedules and rest periods, first aid, contacts of personnel representatives, prevention service, and labor law inspection. Provisions corresponding to items 12° to 19° of Article 124 may be subject to explicit reference to the work rules containing them. Information about the trial period has been mandatory since November 10, 2022.
source: SPF Employment, Labor and Social Dialogue · emploi.belgique.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: From age 15: conditions and light work
summary: Since May 4, 2026, certain 15-year-olds still subject to full-time schooling can perform light work.
body: Child labor remains generally prohibited. At 15, completion of the first two years of secondary school allows exit from full-time schooling obligation; this ends by age 16 at the latest. Before age 15, a regular student job is not permitted.

For 15-year-olds still subject to this obligation, only authorized light activities are suitable: reception, cloakroom, restocking, sales assistance, certain logistics operations, light cleaning, and distribution or clearing of meals in care settings. They cannot require specific training or use of mechanical equipment.

Verify actual tasks before publishing the offer. They must preserve health, development, and schooling; working during classes is excluded. Prior risk analysis required by Article X.3-3 of the Well-Being Code remains mandatory.
source: SPF Employment, Labor and Social Dialogue · emploi.belgique.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: 650 hours per calendar year
summary: In 2026, the permanent social quota is 650 hours across all employers.
body: Working year-round is permitted, excluding mandatory classes. The counter resets to 650 hours each January. Only actually worked hours are counted; ordinary contributions begin at the 651st hour.

Keep proof of current school enrollment: a student card alone is insufficient. After a degree obtained in June, ONSS still accepts the regime until September 30, without disguised trial of regular employment.

title: Student solidarity contribution
summary: Budget the employer contribution and withhold the student portion when reduced regime conditions are met.
body: ONSS 2026/3 instructions set the solidarity contribution at 8.13% of remuneration: 5.42% borne by the employer and 2.71% borne by the student. Prior Dimona STU and compliance with conditions excluding ordinary contributions are essential.

The employer contribution to the Asbestos Fund of 0.01% is added when applicable. The page indicates collection generally in the first and second quarters, subject to different royal decree. Do not present 5.42% as the guaranteed total employer cost for any period.

title: Student at work: check available balance
summary: Request a certificate to check available hours before planning employment with reduced contributions.
body: The reference quota is 650 hours since January 1, 2025. The student downloads their PDF certificate from My Student at work. The code provided to the employer allows checking the balance for three months; other jobs and detailed data remain invisible.

Hours reserved by employers already decrease the balance, even before work is performed. Correct erroneous reservations via Dimona. The certificate remains optional and does not replace verification of student status. In temporary work, the agency may directly check the balance with the student’s written consent.

title: Declare hours in Dimona STU
summary: The STU declaration must precede work and be based on an already-signed student contract.
body: ONSS 2026/3 instructions require one Dimona per quarter covered by the contract, with planned hours. Do not declare a quarter without work or zero hours. Each hour started counts as one full hour in Dimona and DmfA.

Without prior Dimona STU, the solidarity regime is refused for the late-declared period, even if the quota remains available. Change planned hours by the last day of the month following the quarter; after DmfA introduction, this change no longer adjusts the quota.
Declare the actual address of the first workplace when it differs from the registered office. In construction, instructions also require both C3.2 card numbers each quarter.

title: Student status, apprenticeship, and exclusions
summary: Check the training program and schedule before any commitment.
body: ONSS 2026/3 admits recognized apprenticeship, excluding classes and practical training, without unemployment or job-seeker benefits. The student employer must normally be different from the training supervisor.

Exception in July and August when the apprenticeship contract is inactive: the same employer is admitted. Theoretical training only on a part-time basis only allows student work during school holidays. Other evening or reduced-schedule classes are excluded.
After twelve consecutive months with the same employer, ordinary contract rules apply.

title: Student wage and percentages by age
summary: First apply the sectoral collective agreement; age-related student wage reduction has not generally disappeared.
body: Absent an applicable sectoral collective agreement, the SPF publishes the interprofessional minima as of July 1, 2026: 2,233.61 € monthly at 21 years, 2,010.25 € at 20 years, 1,898.57 € at 19 years, 1,764.55 € at 18 years, 1,630.54 € at 17 years, and 1,496.52 € at 16 years.

The corresponding percentages are 100, 90, 85, 79, 73, and 67%. Identify the joint committee before pricing the offer; the general table does not replace its scale. The SPF provides hourly equivalents for 38 hours weekly, including 13.5644 € at 21 years.
source: SPF Employment, Labor and Social Dialogue · emploi.belgique.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Dangerous work and health surveillance
summary: Analyze risks before the student arrives and organize required health surveillance.
body: Book X, Title 3 of the Well-Being Code is the current reference for young worker protection. Article X.3-3: analysis before work, updated at least annually and when there is a significant change. Article X.3-8 and Annex X.3-1 notably prohibit dangerous exposures, processes, and machines.

Article X.3-11: exemption for a student requires notably age 18, studies corresponding to the activity, controlled measures, an experienced worker present, and prior opinion from the prevention adviser and committee. Motorized handling equipment has a special regime under Article X.3-11/1; do not automatically assign a student to a forklift.

Article X.3-12 organizes health surveillance. Arrange for the required prior assessment, notably for minors, night work, and work normally prohibited but authorized by exemption. Safety positions, vigilance roles, or defined-risk positions also require appropriate surveillance.
source: SPF Employment, Labor and Social Dialogue · emploi.belgique.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Minors: schedules, night work, and Sundays
summary: Workers under 18 enjoy additional limits, even when the sector operates evenings or Sundays.
body: For young workers outside full-time schooling obligation, provide a maximum of eight hours per day and 40 hours per week, with 38 actual or average hours since January 1, 2003. Add work with multiple employers and part-time mandatory training.

30-minute break beyond 4.5 hours; beyond six hours, one hour including 30 consecutive minutes, subject to exemptions. Rest between days is at least twelve hours. Work between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. is generally prohibited; exemptions are controlled and never permit work between midnight and 4 a.m.

Sunday and public holidays are generally prohibited. The page notably provides an exemption for retail stores and refers to horeca-specific orders. Even with exemption, exceeding one Sunday in two requires prior authorization from labor law inspection. Organize compensatory rest.
source: SPF Employment, Labor and Social Dialogue · emploi.belgique.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Walloon Region: work and family allowances
summary: For a student under the Walloon system, distinguish the 650 student hours from the 240 quarterly hours at ordinary contribution rates.
body: The FAMIWAL sheet updated June 17, 2026 maintains the right unconditionally until August 31 of the year of 18 years. After that, the young person's activity and situation must comply with the conditions for maintaining the right.

The 650 annual hours at reduced contribution rates do not block allowances. Beyond that, an additional quota of 240 hours per quarter applies to work subject to ordinary contributions. Only actual work counts, not paid public holidays. Check the student's residence regime; this sheet concerns Walloon allowances, not those of the German-speaking Community.

title: Flemish Region: 650 hours and monthly ceiling
summary: Groeipakket distinguishes the student quota from the monthly ceiling applicable to other work.
body: For students aged 18 to 25, the student ceiling is 650 hours per year at reduced contribution rates. The change to 650 hours took effect January 1, 2025. Up to 80 hours per month can be added at ordinary contribution rates.

Hours exceeding the student quota count toward these 80 hours. If this monthly ceiling is exceeded, Groeipakket is lost for that month. Maintenance also requires other regime conditions, notably regarding social benefits. Notify the fund of any change in employment situation.

title: Brussels: 240-hour ceiling per quarter
summary: The 650-hour social quota does not guarantee maintenance of Brussels family allowances.
body: Under the Brussels regime effective January 2020, the right is unconditional until August 31 of the year of 18 years. After that, a student under 25 can work without losing allowances if their activity does not exceed 240 hours per quarter.

Exceeding the limit results in loss of allowances for the entire quarter. In the third quarter, July to September, the ceiling does not apply if the young person continues studies after summer. Verify this continuation before promising a graduating student summer work without impact.

title: 2026 income: tax and parental tax burden
summary: Tax thresholds are distinct from the social quota.
body: For 2026 income, Student at work indicates 15,971.43 € to avoid paying tax and 22,385 € to remain a tax dependent. These are gross amounts after deduction of social contributions, not contractual gross amounts.

These benchmarks assume only student job income and standard professional expenses. With other resources or actual expenses, have the situation recalculated by SPF Finance. The student must file a return even below the tax threshold.

title: Students outside EEA: residence and work limit
summary: The right to work depends on residence status. The 20-hour rule applies in all three regions for affected student residence permits.
body: The SPF distinguishes federal authorizations linked to residence from regional economic migration authorizations. Citizens of the EEA and Switzerland are authorized to work. For a third-country national admitted to reside as a student with a valid limited permit, check the residence document before hiring.

The Royal Decree of September 2, 2018 permits work during school holidays; outside holidays, work cannot exceed twenty hours per week and must remain compatible with studies. Do not confuse this limit with the annual social quota. Students admitted under European mobility programs are also covered under the residence conditions indicated on the page.
source: SPF Employment, Labor and Social Dialogue · emploi.belgique.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: CP 124: student minimum since July 2026
summary: The official July 2026 table sets a student hourly minimum specific to construction.
body: Section 6 of the CP 124 scale, effective July 1, 2026 and updated July 7, indicates 16.1755 € gross per hour for students. Reserve this scale for workers under this joint committee.

The collective agreement of March 19, 2026, linked to the page, replaces Article 10 of the collective agreement of June 12, 2014: base of 16 € as of April 1, 2026, regardless of employment period, indexed each July 1. The introductory note still mentioning alignment with Category I since 2024 does not describe this new regime. Use the updated student section and the amending collective agreement.
source: SPF Employment, Labor and Social Dialogue · salairesminimums.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Horeca: combining student and occasional work
summary: The two quotas can be combined without stacking benefits on the same work.
body: The 650-hour regime established in 2025 remains distinct from the 50 annual days of horeca occasional work. The student and employer agree on which regime to use.

Occasional work limits the contract to two successive days and calculates contributions on a flat rate. Check Horeca@work for available days and Student at work for student hours. A student contract remains required if its conditions are met.
